title: SharePoint Lists: refreshed command bar, view selection and filter pills on the web
summary: Hold: the release-preferences instructions omit Microsoft's rollout qualification and the alternative route for tenants without the new admin experience. The roadmap facts and SharePoint licensing are supported; the discussion of custom command-bar buttons also needs its supporting reference.

claims.claim: Administrators can configure Deferred release through Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Release preferences > Deferred release without a rollout qualification.
claims.quote: The unified release preferences experience is rolling out gradually in mid-November 2026, so it might not be available in your organization yet. ... If the unified release preferences experience hasn't rolled out to your organization yet, you can still manage release options following these steps:
claims.fix: Keep the printed path but qualify it in the row note and the Before rollout instruction: 'This route requires the unified release preferences experience, rolling out gradually from mid-November 2026. If it is not available in your tenant, use Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot Release Preferences: General Availability > Deferred release.' Both routes and the rollout condition are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/configure-release-options.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API or PowerShell operation to set Standard or Deferred release preferences.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Deferred release Standard release release preferences Microsoft Graph API PowerShell configure users'; read Configure new Standard and Deferred release options and the returned Graph user-properties excerpt. No release-preference write operation was documented.

claims.claim: Deferred release delays deferred-eligible major updates for assigned users by approximately 30 days after Standard rollout begins.

claims.claim: Deferred release does not delay updates that are not eligible for deferral.

claims.claim: Release preferences control delivery timing of eligible updates rather than permanently preventing their delivery.
claims.quote: After the 30-day period, deferred-eligible features are released to users in the Deferred release audience.
